nodes.name: TrainingArea
nodes.purpose: Plain flat floor, spawn point and fixed dummy placement point defining the walkable practice space; default Roblox camera and movement apply, no boundaries or decoration.

nodes.name: DummyModel
nodes.purpose: Stationary target dummy providing hitbox geometry and appearance for punch registration; has no behavior, health, or reaction of its own.

nodes.name: PunchAnimationAsset
nodes.purpose: R15 forward jab animation clip (windup/strike/recovery, clip 1/1/18/1) played on the player's Animator when a punch is approved.

nodes.name: PunchImpactSoundAsset
nodes.purpose: One-shot punch impact sound instance played on server-confirmed hits.

nodes.name: PunchInputController
nodes.purpose: Captures the single punch input (click/Space/gamepad A), gates re-trigger while mid-punch, and requests a punch from the server; plays the approved animation and rebinds on respawn.

nodes.name: PunchServer
nodes.purpose: Authoritative punch handler: validates cooldown/mid-punch state and player health, checks strike-window overlap against the dummy hitbox, and coordinates approved-animation playback, hit confirmation, sound trigger and counter increment.

nodes.name: HitDetectionModule
nodes.purpose: Shared per-player cooldown/mid-punch state tracking plus the distance/hitbox overlap math used to decide exactly one hit per swing.

nodes.name: HitCounterService
nodes.purpose: Tracks each player's session hit count keyed by UserId and replicates updates to that player's HUD; cleans up on PlayerRemoving.

nodes.name: HitCounterHud
nodes.purpose: Displays the persistent 'Hits: N' on-screen counter anchored to a fixed screen corner; has no reset control and survives respawns.

edges.effect: Client sends a punch request when the input is pressed and the client-side mid-punch flag is clear.
Server asks HitDetectionModule to check the player's cooldown state and distance/hitbox overlap with the dummy.
Returns approved/denied and hit/miss result gated by a per-swing single-hit flag.
Reads the dummy's fixed hitbox part CFrame/size to test strike-window overlap.
Tells the client to play the forward jab animation in sync with the server-authoritative swing.
Client plays the R15 punch animation clip 1/1/18/1 via the character's Animator on approval.
On a confirmed hit, the server triggers the punch impact Sound instance near the dummy so playback replicates to the client.
On a confirmed hit, the server increments that player's session hit count exactly once per swing.
Server replicates the new count to the player's client, which updates the 'Hits: N' label.
Player spawns on the plain floor near the dummy using the default avatar/camera/movement; the input controller rebinds to the new character.
Dummy is placed at a fixed point on the floor within comfortable punching range of spawn.

assetNeeds.role: Stationary training dummy providing the target's appearance and hitbox for punch registration
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to the user-selected asset 1245720733 (Training Dummy by Xtrah962). Verify it is a stationary, non-humanoid-controlled prop with no health/damage/AI loop. Identify a clear hitbox part usable for server distance/overlap checks. Inspect its 1 embedded script and report/exclude any behavior that would move, flinch, or animate the dummy, since the approved design requires it to remain purely stationary and non-reactive.

intent.experienceRole: The sole punchable target that gives the player a concrete goal to walk to and strike; its fixed presence anchors the entire training-drill loop.
intent.interaction: Non-interactive prop for positioning purposes only; the player's punch strike-window overlaps its hitbox to register a hit server-side, but the dummy itself never reacts, moves, flinches, or attacks.
reusableFeatures: Existing red/black canvas heavy-bag mesh and stand/base geometry
A distinguishable torso/body part usable as the hit-detection hitbox
Inspection of the embedded script to confirm it does not add movement, damage, or AI behavior that must be disabled

assetNeeds.role: R15-compatible forward jab punch animation clip for the player's avatar
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to the user-selected asset 12061946559 (R15 Punching Animations by Auevi). Locate the embedded clip at key 1/1/18/1 specifically. Verify R15 rig compatibility with the default Roblox avatar and a duration of roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds covering windup/strike/recovery. Extract a usable Animation/AnimationId reference for Animator playback. Report, rather than execute, any packaged behavior script unrelated to the animation data itself.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the core visual feedback that makes each punch read as a deliberate player action distinct from idle movement, central to the requested fighting-game feel.
intent.interaction: Played once per server-approved punch input, timed to the authoritative strike window; purely presentational and does not itself decide hit success.
reusableFeatures: The specific embedded clip at key 1/1/18/1
Any keyframe markers indicating strike-frame timing useful for syncing the server hit-check window
Confirmation of R15 Animator/AnimationController compatibility with the default avatar rig

assetNeeds.role: Punch/hit impact sound effect played once per successful connect
assetNeeds.constraints: Must resolve to the user-selected asset 132504023010884 (Punch Impact 1 by NickySergal). Verify it loads and plays correctly as a Sound instance parented near the dummy's hitbox, triggered server-side so playback replicates to the client. Confirm it is a short one-shot 'thwack'-style connect sound, not a whiff/miss variant, and pass load/playback/listening checks before acceptance.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers the auditory payoff confirming a successful hit, reinforcing the arcade-boxing 'thwack' feel called for in the approved theme.
intent.interaction: Plays exactly once per confirmed successful punch connection, synchronized with the hit-counter increment; not ambient or decorative audio.
reusableFeatures: The single verified one-shot audio clip
Any loudness/tone characteristics worth preserving for a satisfying impact feel

assetStrategy: Three Marketplace assets were already selected by the user and must be preserved and integrated rather than replaced: (1) 'Training Dummy' (1245720733) supplies the stationary target's full appearance and geometry - its single embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep or disable it, since the requirement is a purely stationary, non-reactive dummy; (2) 'R15 Punching Animations' (12061946559) supplies the forward jab clip at embedded key 1/1/18/1, which must be located, verified as R15-compatible with the default avatar, and exposed for Animator playback - per the standalone-animation limitation, this is sourced as a Model pack rather than a bare Animation asset; (3) 'Punch Impact 1' (132504023010884) supplies the one-shot hit sound, which must be verified for load/playback/listening before being wired to the server's hit-confirmation path. No additional decorative, environment, or animation Marketplace searches are needed given the deliberately minimal scope (plain floor, default avatar, default camera). Missing integration work is limited to: parenting/positioning the dummy and its hitbox reference, extracting and playing the specific punch clip on server-approved requests, and triggering/parenting the impact sound near the dummy for server-controlled playback. All hit validation, cooldown, and counter logic are original small server-authoritative scripts/modules, since no Marketplace behavior was selected or requested for those systems.
title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The full punch loop works end to end: pressing the single punch input while not mid-punch triggers a server-approved punch, plays the animation, checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy, and on success plays the sound and increments the counter.
requirements.sourceQuote: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the punch input (left click / Space / gamepad A) while not mid-punch produces a full observable cycle: server approval, client animation playback, server hit-window check against the dummy, and on success a synchronized sound plus a +1 counter update, reproducible across repeated swings with correct cooldown gating.

requirements.description: The player cannot chain or spam punches: a punch action can only start if the player is not already mid-punch, and only one hit registers per swing even if dummy overlap persists across multiple frames.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.
requirements.acceptance: Server rejects a new RequestPunch while the player's per-player mid-punch/cooldown flag is true; a per-swing hit-registered flag ensures at most one hit is counted per swing regardless of how long strike-window overlap with the dummy lasts.

requirements.description: An approved punch plays the selected forward jab animation (clip key 1/1/18/1 from asset 12061946559) on the player's avatar, lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds with windup, strike and recovery phases.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

requirements.description: A plain, undecorated flat floor holds the fixed dummy placement point and a spawn point a short walk away, with no arena decoration or props.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.
requirements.acceptance: A single flat floor Part exists with no additional props or backdrop; the dummy sits at a fixed point and the spawn point is placed a short walk from it, with no invisible walls or boundary parts added.

requirements.acceptance: PunchServer checks the requesting player's Humanoid, current cooldown/mid-punch flag, and distance/overlap against the dummy hitbox server-side before approving a punch or confirming a hit; no hit/miss/timestamp claim from the client is trusted directly.

requirements.description: The experience is single-player focused with no AI opponent behavior; if multiple players are present, each player's cooldown and hit count are tracked independently.
requirements.acceptance: No AI opponent, PvP, or cross-player interference exists; per-player cooldown state and hit counts are keyed by UserId so concurrent players do not affect each other's counters.

requirements.description: Per-player server state and client-side connections are cleaned up and rebound correctly on player leave and character respawn, avoiding stale state or duplicate HUDs.
requirements.acceptance: On PlayerRemoving, the player's cooldown state and hit-count entry are removed from server tables; on CharacterAdded, the client's input/animation controller and HUD rebind to the new character without duplicating connections or creating a stale duplicate counter display.
